stories.headline: COP31 ends without a deal after EU rejects text omitting fossil fuels

sources.body:
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.

Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.

But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.

The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed".

He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he said were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

"That is the reality," he said on Monday.

After two weeks of negotiations, exhausted delegates were presented with a new, draft deal in the early hours of Sunday to try to break the deadlock.

But the words "fossil fuels" did not appear anywhere in the text. The only indirect reference to coal, oil and gas was a nod to a deal agreed at COP28 in 2023 , when countries agreed to "transition away" from fossil fuels in energy systems.

The EU's representative, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien, made it clear that the EU "strongly" objected, saying that the "decisions go nowhere near the level of ambition needed to tackle climate change".

"It is unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no mention of fossil fuels," he said.

Other countries, such as Panama and the Marshall Islands, also criticised the deal for doing nowhere near enough to tackle the pace of climate change.

A first draft of the deal on Monday mentioned "fossil fuel" or "fossil fuels" six times, but that was unacceptable to oil-producing nations.

Saudi Arabia's delegate Mohammad Ayoub said that Arab countries "continued to engage in good faith" but argued that they only accounted for a small proportion of historical greenhouse gas emissions.

Russia warned not to "turn to slogans" over coal, oil and gas, claiming that if countries moved away from fossil fuels too quickly it would lead to "fuel poverty".

Another major sticking point has been money for poorer countries to adapt to the impacts of climate change, such as more intense heatwaves and more severe droughts.

Last year at COP30 in Brazil , nations agreed to triple the finance for that purpose.

But this year's deal contained no reference to concrete figures, nor the baseline against which that pledge would be measured. This raised fears it would give richer nations too much wriggle room.
sources.headline: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions

sources.body:
EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels

The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey .

The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required. [It] does not even mention fossil fuels.”

As the talks, scheduled to end on Friday, dragged on into Sunday afternoon in the longest climate summit ever, it was clear that the “Antalya pact”, drafted by the Turkish and Australian joint presidencies of the summit, would not achieve the consensus needed to pass.

The Antalya pact invites countries to electrify their economies, calls for rich countries to provide finance to the poor to help them adapt to the impacts of the climate crisis, and calls on countries to minimise the “overshoot” of the 1.5C global heating threshold, of the Paris agreement.

But it failed to endorse the “transition away from fossil fuels” that more than 130 countries demanded, and included controversial provisions on “carbon capture and storage” (CCS) technology that some have said perpetuates fossil fuels.

The presidencies avoided outright collapse of the “conference of the parties” by passing decisions on various related matters, including the “just transition” to help workers in high-carbon industries shift to a low-carbon economy.

But Murat Kurum, Turkey’s Cop president, acknowledged there was no agreement on the draft “cover decision” text and so it had not been adopted.

“We have done our utmost; ultimately, we have not imposed this text on anyone, nor have we issued an ultimatum ⁠such as a ‘take it or leave it’ demand,” he said. “It is clear that there are parties in this hall who oppose this text. We recognise ⁠that there is no consensus on this document. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted.”

Many countries, including the EU, UK and developing countries including small island states and some of the poorest countries, said they could not support the Antalya pact deal, which was supposed to be main outcome of the Cop.

In a dramatic intervention, O’Brien said on behalf of the EU that it could not accept the final text in its current form. “It fails to meet the moment … We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.” He said the EU would not accept a decision “that greenwashes fossil fuels”.

His intervention was met by applause from the hall, and was later followed by similar objections from Panama, the Marshall Islands and Norway.

“This feels like a real line in the sand moment. Countries are standing up to fossil fuel interests and saying no,” said Bill Hare, the chief executive of the advisory group Climate Analytics.
sources.headline: Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected

stories.headline: Tankers set ablaze in Strait of Hormuz as Iran escalates Gulf attacks

sources.body: Iran’s navy claims tankers contravening its rules were set ablaze, while the IRGC said ‘enemies’ sought to stoke unrest.
sources.headline: Tankers set ablaze in Hormuz as IRGC warns of unrest threat

sources.body:
Tehran has ramped up attacks in recent days as the US naval blockade and sanctions campaign hurt the country economically.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed to have targeted radars at a United States military base in Bahrain, as Iran has intensified attacks over the past week, hitting tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, a global oil chokepoint, and downing US drones.

At least 25 tankers have been hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas passes, in the past seven days, causing the Gulf oil flow to drop sharply.

The escalating attacks come as Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country is facing what he called a “silent economic war” amid US sanctions and a naval blockade.

So what is behind Iran’s latest escalation, and will it trigger a new round of hostilities between Tehran and Washington or force the two sides to sit down for talks to end the war that has caused a global energy crisis?

Bahrain has faced the brunt of Iran’s attacks in recent days.

On Saturday, Manama said an Iranian strike hit a civilian industrial facility, starting a fire , as it thwarted several other attacks that day.

The IRGC said it had carried out a combined missile and drone operation targeting US military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, claiming to have destroyed two US Patriot air defence radars at the bases.

Iranian state media reported that an interceptor missile launched from the US Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain crashed on Sitra Island near Manama, sparking a large fire.

The IRGC said the operation was retaliation for a US strike on a radar installation on Iran’s Hengam Island. Iran has justified the attacks as a response to continued violations of its airspace, including by US MQ-1 and MQ-9 reconnaissance and combat drones.

Bahrain has faced three drone attacks in recent days after a lull in fighting for several weeks.

Iran’s army on Saturday said its air defences fired a missile at a US F-16 jet over the Gulf the previous evening, damaging the aircraft, the IRNA news agency reported. However, US Central Command (CENTCOM) denied the claim, stating that “all US fighter jets in the Middle East are safe and accounted for”.

Iranian forces on Sunday also said they shot down another MQ-1 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC claimed it was the 20th US drone of this type to be shot down since the war began in late February and the fourth in the past 24 hours.

Meanwhile, British maritime authorities reported two incidents involving tankers struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman.

Al Jazeera correspondent in Tehran, Resul Serdar, said incidents involving tankers had increased sharply over the past week, with about 25 since November 14.

Last week, the Iranian army also said it targeted US drone and missile installations at Kuwait’s Ali Al Salem base. The attack came after the US struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, which remains under effective Iranian control.

Oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz has seen a considerable dip as Iran has escalated attacks on a near-daily basis.
sources.headline: What’s behind Iran’s escalation of attacks in the Gulf?

stories.headline: Russian warship hit in suspected drone attack at Libya’s Benghazi port

sources.body:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.

The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.

Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press.

Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine , marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war.

Though Ukraine began the war with no navy, it has developed a sea drone capability that threatened Russian warships in the Black Sea. The Russian fleet has been forced to retreat to the eastern port of Novorossiysk because Sevastopol in occupied Crimea had become unsafe.

Hours later, a Russia-linked cargo ship said to be carrying military supplies, the Ascalon, was hit by a sea drone off the coast of Benghazi. Video showed the drone heading directly towards one end of the vessel, again causing a huge explosion.

Libyan naval forces ‌rescued the vessel’s crew, the ‌sources added. The health ministry said some crew members were in stable condition with minor injuries. The number of injured and their nationalities are not known.

Benghazi is controlled by the self-styled Libyan National Army, led by Gen Khalifa Haftar, which controls eastern and southern Libya and has been aligned with Russia.

There was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities, and no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range attacks against Russia far beyond the frontlines.

The UN mission in Libya (Unsmil) expressed “serious concern” over the two drone attacks off Benghazi and called for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”, in a post on X.

The ‌eastern-based Libyan authority said port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that ​normal operations would resume once the fire was brought under control and the site secured.

It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and ⁠a threat to maritime safety, saying it would take ​legal and ​diplomatic measures against ​anyone found responsible.

“The Libyan government will not ​allow Libyan ‌ports, territory or territorial ​waters ​to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.

The specialist website Naval News earlier identified the ship attacked as the Merkury, a Russian corvette – the smallest class of warship, smaller than a frigate – and said it had almost certainly been destroyed.
sources.headline: Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack

sources.body:
There was no immediate reaction from Russia, and no one has claimed responsibility for the suspected attack.

A suspected sea drone attack has hit a Russian vessel in eastern Libya, causing an explosion and a brief fire, according to the North African country’s eastern-based government.

Local sources told Al Jazeera late on Sunday that an unknown number of Libyan and Russian nationals were killed in the attack at dawn, adding that the ship was moored inside the civil sea port of Benghazi, close to a naval base.

The sources said the ship was carrying weapons, ammunition and drones in its cargo. Local sources quoted residents as saying they saw three drones attack the vessel.

Satellite imagery provider Vantor said imagery showed the vessel was the Merkury, a Russian Navy corvette, or small warship.

Imagery taken on Sunday showed that most of the vessel ‌had capsized and sunk, with only its bow still visible above water. Smoke was also visible rising from part of the ship’s superstructure, with significant debris scattered along the pier.

The Benghazi-based administration earlier said the vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement between Russia and Libya’s eastern government.

Late on Sunday, the Associated Press news agency quoted unnamed sources as saying that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya.

Also on Sunday evening, a sea drone hit a Malta-flagged commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack. The Benghazi-based administration’s Health Ministry said all crew members “who were injured when a merchant vessel was targeted this evening by explosives-laden sea drones off the coast of Benghazi” had been rescued and were receiving treatment.

No further details were given. The Almasar satellite television channel said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.

The Benghazi-based administration said it has launched a joint investigation with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it”.

The government said the fire had been brought under control and the site secured, while it condemned the suspected strike as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety.

“The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said, adding that Libya was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have repeatedly used naval drones and missiles to target Russian warships and naval facilities in the Black Sea.

On Saturday, a drone struck a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea near Finnish waters. Finland’s border guard attributed the strike to Ukraine.

A Russian liquefied natural gas carrier sank off the Libyan coast in March after an attack that Russian President Vladimir Putin blamed on Ukraine. Last December, Ukraine said it had used aerial drones to strike a Russian-linked oil tanker in the Mediterranean.
sources.headline: Russian vessel hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Libya’s Benghazi port

sources.body: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a suspected Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, in what appeared to be the latest attack linked to the Russia-Ukraine war in the North African nation. Hours later, a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack off Benghazi on Sunday evening.
sources.headline: Russian warship hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say

stories.headline: UK-EU food deal welcomed by British businesses as Burnham prepares to address Parliament

sources.body:
Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long

British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products.

The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks.

The agreement is due to take effect on 1 March 2028 and is also intended to reopen the EU market for UK products including fresh sausages, burgers, seed potatoes and molluscs.

However, several years after the UK left the bloc, upending many decades-old trading arrangements, some food exporters said they would remain cautious until the deal came into force.

“Nobody’s going to believe this until it has actually physically happened,” said Iain Barbour, the operations director of the Scottish seed potato producer Jamieson Brothers.

Seed potatoes were not included in the post-Brexit trade deal after the two sides disagreed over certification, halting exports from the UK to the EU despite Scottish seed potatoes’ high health status classification.

The exclusion particularly hit the Scottish industry, whose farmers were among the biggest exporters for the production of chips and crisps in the world , as well as growers in northern England. Scottish seed potato farmers previously accounted for three-quarters of UK production and the sector was worth about £112m a year.

Ireland and the EU represented a fifth of Jamieson Brothers’ trade before Brexit . The company particularly suffered from the loss of the Irish business, given it grew many varieties that were popular on plates in the north and south of Ireland.

While the company adapted its business to start packing work that would have previously been carried out in the EU, Barbour estimates this change cost about £500,000.

“We evolved, we worked with more partners and that’s what kept the business going,” Barbour said.

Barbour is looking forward to supplying his Irish customers once againHowever, he said it would take at least three years until he could revive varieties that were no longer being grown and were instead stored in a seed bank.

“A lot of Scottish farmers stopped producing varieties that were popular in Ireland as they weren’t desired in England. Varieties that had been going about 100 years were killed off in a couple of years,” he said. “So we’ll have to look at bringing them back.”

The planned implementation of the food deal in March 2028 would also be “a couple of months late for the trade”, given most sales happen at the start of the year and the crops needs to be grown in advance.

Barbour anticipates most growers will be wary and will only fully resume trading in 2029. “People are obviously going to be a little bit hesitant to grow anything until it’s 100% official,” he said.
sources.headline: UK-EU food deal hailed by British firms: ‘We’re pretty aligned anyway’

sources.body:
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.

The deal is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.

He will also call it "the single biggest growth measure to be delivered in this parliament" - repeating his claim it could add £17bn to the British economy.

The PM described it on Friday as a "win-win" deal with the EU on British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. But since then a host of politicians have criticised the plan, with one former prime minister urging him to "move on" from Brexit.

Burnham believes the agreement reached in Brussels "holds out the very real prospect that the next decade can be a much better one for Britain than the one we have just lived through".

"The ability to draw a line on a decade of drift and division is in our hands and I believe we should take it," he will say in his speech.

He will also paint the move as a choice "between easing pressure on the cost of living or allowing food prices to rise further" and "creating opportunities for young people or denying them".

He believes polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".

But his announcement on Friday was greeted with a chorus of criticism from a number of opposing political figures.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal was unfair because UK farmers would now have to follow rules made by Brussels.

She questioned the Treasury's analysis, which Burnham said suggested the deal "will add up to 0.5%" to UK gross domestic product and he described it as a "£17bn boost to the British economy".

Badenoch accused him of having "plucked that figure out of the air" before saying "the only modelling I've seen that even talks about that figure says it's actually 0.0%".

Meanwhile Reform UK leader Farage called the deal a "very good day for the EU", before adding: "A good day to try and humiliate the one member state that actually had the courage to say, 'We don't need to be part of you, we can govern our own country'."

Farage, who was a leading figure in the 2016 campaign to get Britain out of the EU, added in a social media post: "Like every prime minister before him, Burnham is a total fraud. Only Reform will stop the endless betrayal of the British people."

Over the weekend former prime ministers including Theresa May, Sir Tony Blair and Rishi Sunak also criticised the EU-UK deal.

May, who presided over three years of Brexit negotiations during her premiership, said she was "aghast" by the deal and warned Andy Burnham should "move on".

Sir Tony, who was a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, told The Sunday Times Britain should only rejoin the EU if it reforms, and allows more innovation on technology.

Badenoch will use her speech at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) annual conference on Monday to criticise Burnham's EU deal.
sources.headline: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'

stories.headline: Russian strike destroys apartment building near Kyiv, killing at least two

sources.body: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.
sources.headline: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv

sources.body:
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer after 14 hours, in overnight Russian strikes on Dymer, in the Kyiv region, that killed ten people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.

Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.

Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.

Response teams including police, explosive technicians, dog handlers and medics are continuing with rescue efforts.

In a telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.

Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

Zelensky said more than 130 people are involved in emergency operations at the scene, and that they will continue until they have "complete information about every single person".

Sending his condolences to the families and loved ones of those killed, he said the strike struck the residential building, "practically blowing a section of it to smithereens".

Zelensky added that "rescue efforts are complicated by constant new air raid alerts and renewed threats".

The strike hit the building at 05:00 local time, when families were still asleep, Ukraine's minister of internal affairs Ivan Vyhivskyi said.

More than 70 strikes have been launched across 10 Ukrainian regions as of Sunday evening, Vyhivskyi added.

In his video address posted online, Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 injured in a strike on an "ordinary grocery store" in Vyshneve.

Mayor Illya Dikov wrote on social media that three children were among the injured.

Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said in a post on X.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
sources.headline: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say

stories.headline: Indonesian factory fire leaves dozens missing as police recover 24 body bags

sources.body:
Authorities in Java are searching for dozens of missing workers as they continue to battle remaining hotspots.

Indonesian authorities are set to resume the search for missing workers on Monday after police removed 24 body bags from a factory in Java gutted by a fire.

Firefighters continued to battle remaining hotspots on Sunday after the blaze broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, Serang regency, West Java province.

A search for dozens of missing workers was suspended overnight but would resume Monday morning, Hendra Kurniawan, the police chief of Indonesia’s Banten province, told local broadcaster Metro TV on Sunday.

Steven Erwin Wijaya, the CEO of the factory’s parent company, PT United Family Food, said at a news conference that about 300 people were present for Saturday’s shift, with 65 of them believed to have been in the affected area when the fire broke out.

In a statement that followed, the factory said 24 of the 65 workers had returned home, four were receiving medical treatment, 29 remained ‌missing, and the whereabouts of another eight had yet to be confirmed.

At a news conference on Sunday, Wahyu Hidayati Dwi Palupi, a police disaster victim identification official, said the intensity of the fire had made it impossible to identify the recovered victims visually. She said they would collect DNA samples from relatives and the personal belongings of the missing workers, a process that could take two to three weeks.

The number of dead was not immediately clear. Police said that one body bag could contain parts ⁠of more than one person.

Authorities said the cause of the fire was being investigated. Parts of the building remained at risk of collapse, an official added.

Photos and videos circulating online on Sunday showed flames and thick smoke coming from the factory, which borders the capital, Jakarta. Footage from inside the three-storey building appeared to show the fire caused extensive damage, with equipment blackened and destroyed.

Indonesia has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.

A fire in an office building in Jakarta killed at least 22 people last December. An explosion at an Indonesian nickel-processing plant killed at least 13 people in 2023.
sources.headline: Indonesian police remove 24 body bags from factory fire site

sources.body:
Relatives of the missing victims flocked to the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones

A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36 remaining missing, an Indonesian rescue official says.

Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex. Photos and videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims on Sunday, with small fires still burning in some spots.

Relatives of the missing victims flocked near the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones, footage aired by local broadcasters showed.

The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in Cikande in Indonesia’s Banten province about 50km from the capital, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, search and rescue official Rizky Dwianto said on Sunday.

“All elements of the joint SAR [search-and-rescue] team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritising the safety of personnel in the field,” he added.

Rizky said four people were injured and taken to a nearby hospital and health clinic.

Firefighters were alerted about 4.30pm on Saturday and found the building already engulfed in flames when they arrived, fire official Tubagus Machfudz told local broadcaster Kompas TV.

“When we arrived … a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company’s protection system was functioning properly or not,” he said.

The Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters overnight that an estimated 60 people were inside the factory when it caught fire.

The cause of the incident is still under investigation, the local disaster agency said in an Instagram post on Sunday.

Deadly fires are not uncommon in Indonesia.

In December last year, a blaze that was likely caused by a drone battery explosion tore through a seven-storey building in Jakarta and killed at least 22 people, police said.

In 2023, at least 13 people were killed in the country’s east after an explosion at a nickel-processing plant.
sources.headline: Fire at confectionery factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing

sources.body:
At least three people have been killed after a fire at a confectionery factory in western Java on Saturday, with the death toll expected to rise.

Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for around 36 missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.

Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries.

Rescuers recovered 24 body bags from the fire as of Sunday evening, as search operations continue to locate missing people.

Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire on Saturday evening.

The factory is in Serang district, Banten province, about 50km (31km) west of Jakarta. Authorities have not yet determined the fire's cause.

Photos and footage of the scene showed the large factory taken over by flames during the night, firefighters battling the flames, and first responders retrieving at least one body from the wreckage on Sunday morning.

Local media reported that the search had been called off for the night late on Sunday, and would resume on Monday.

"All members of the joint SAR team are making every effort to locate the missing victims while prioritising the safety of personnel on the ground," the rescue agency said.

Relatives of the missing workers had gathered outside the factory waiting for updates, according to local broadcasts cited by AFP.

Firefighters had been called to the building at 16:30 local time (09:30 GMT) on Saturday - but it was already engulfed in flames, broadcaster Kompas TV reported, citing fire official Tubugas Machfudz.

"When we arrived (on location)... a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company's protection system was functioning properly or not," he said.

The factory is owned by PT Fonusa Agung Mulia, according to search and rescue authorities.

On LinkedIn the company describes itself as a subsidiary of UNIFAM, one of Indonesia's largest food and beverage companies.
sources.headline: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory

stories.headline: South Korea’s education minister resigns amid AI exam-cheating scandal

sources.body:
South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation.

He said he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung.

A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone and AI tools. This prompted officials to act urgently to detect hidden devices, including sending emergency alerts to every single mobile phone in the country.

The Suneung takes up to nine hours to complete, and it plays a big role in career trajectories of millions of South Koreans.

"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier said 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

Concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

These fears came to a boil last weekend, when Han Won-seok, the top tax accountancy exam scorer in April, admitted to cheating.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," the 34-year-old said in a video message.

This prompted the authorities to introduce urgent measures, with just days ahead of the Suneung.

This included sending nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea used its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told Yonhap he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.
sources.headline: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal

sources.body:
Choi Kyo-jin says he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams following last-minute scramble to tighten measures

South Korea’s education minister has resigned after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted in the lead-up to key university entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, when the top scorer in a national tax accountancy exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial university entrance exam, known as the suneung .

The cheat’s confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures for the university entrance exams, including blocking public wifi in testing areas.

The unprecedented crackdown included doubling the number of supervisors and sending emergency alerts to detect any smartphones illegally smuggled into the exam centres.

Students were also told to turn up with pencils only. Erasers were provided by the test centres, as authorities tried to reduce the chances of concealed digital devices disguised as stationery.

In addition, exam-takers were asked to avoid wearing clothes with buttons. Those who failed to comply were told they would have stickers placed over the buttons to prevent the use of hidden cameras.

The government promised a reward of at least $75,000 (£57,300) for anyone reporting cheating or misconduct, with reduced penalties for those who turned in their accomplices.

But the education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, struggled to reassure the public, and teachers’ unions criticised the government response as belated.

“The exam concluded without any major incidents … However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance,” Choi wrote on X. “Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation.”

The president, Lee Jae Myung, accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

The annual, eight-hour suneung determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects. It is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, Choi, 72, replied: “Due to my age, I am not confident I could.” His response quickly drew a public backlash.

Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday’s exam, and a vice-minister instead announced the preventive measures.

The person who cheated in the national tax accountancy exam said in a video posted to his lawyer’s YouTube account that he had photographed the questions with a concealed microcamera, sent them to an AI system and read the answers from a smartphone. “I cheated in the tax accountant exam,” he said. “My top placing is not the result of legitimate effort.”
sources.headline: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams

sources.body: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday following a major cheating scandal that erupted just ahead of the country’s university entrance exams. The controversy centred on the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam, who admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to secure a near-perfect result. Jack Pownall reports.
sources.headline: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos

stories.headline: North Carolina recount win gives Democrats their largest House majority since 1992

sources.body:
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.

Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

Sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.

"I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change," Hubbard told the BBC News Channel after his victory. He pledged to work alongside his fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Earlier, he wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

Hubbard added: "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District."

Foxx, meanwhile, said in a statement: "After running a campaign focused on my track record of commonsense solutions and conservative values, I'm humbled and grateful that so many North Carolina voters responded by supporting my candidacy, even if we came up just a few votes short."

Hubbard's win, which comes after he lost to Foxx in the 2024 midterms by nine percentage points, followed a number of Democratic victories in deeply Republican districts including South Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Iowa.

Hubbard, like many Democrats running in the midterms, focused on the rising cost of living in the US during the war with Iran - a top issue for voters.

Trump himself - as well as Vice President JD Vance - have suggested inflation caused by the war in Iran was probably to blame for the Republican losses.

Hubbard has also said he will also prioritise working families and small businesses, supporting public education and expanding access to affordable healthcare, according to his website.

The remaining House races yet to be called are in Tennessee and Minnesota, while two elections in Louisiana will go to a runoff in December. In Tennessee's fourth district, Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than 300 votes, and in Minnesota's first district, Democrat Jake Johnson is winning by fewer than 500 votes.

Democrats may use their upcoming majority in the House and control of the Senate to investigate conflicts of interest and other actions by the president and those close to him, while the Senate also has the power to confirm or block the president's cabinet and judicial nominations. They will also be able to pass legislation through Congress easily, though Trump still has to give final sign off for it to become law.
sources.headline: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat

sources.body: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.
sources.headline: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority

stories.headline: US Army says it will proceed with Iowa explosives detonation despite court order

sources.body: The Trump administration says an emergency provision allows it proceed despite a pending lawsuit by environmental groups.
sources.headline: U.S. Army tells court it will go ahead with detonation in Iowa by Tuesday

sources.body:
The US Army plans to move ahead with detonating five tonnes of degraded explosives in Iowa despite a ruling to halt it indefinitely, a new court filing shows.

"To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action," the justice department notified the court on Saturday. "Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay."

The court had ordered a pause after environmental groups sued to stop the detonation, arguing the army failed to consider safer alternatives.

The detonation was originally scheduled for Friday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The army now plans to act by 24 November under an emergency exemption.

In the new filing, the Department of the Army argued that a controlled detonation was necessary to protect the public from an unplanned explosion, a risk it said would become more likely as temperatures were set to fall in the coming days.

"There is an immediate risk that the lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant will explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1C) in the next several days," the filing states.

It argued that the army had removed the doors to the bunker where the barrels were stored in preparation for the detonation and that made the explosives more "vulnerable to temperature changes".

The government has not released details for the rescheduled detonation.

Earlier, the army had warned residents to leave their homes for six hours on the original scheduled day of the explosion, for the duration of the explosion and until the dust settled. An advisory warned "all humans" to avoid being outside in the affected areas while the demolition detonation was set to take place.

Lead azide is a highly volatile compound used as a detonator. Earlier this year, the IAAAP found that the material had degraded over time to the point where it was now too risky to move the material, according to Iowa Public Radio.

On Friday, the military said it was working with the Department of Health and Human Services and the EPA to ensure the explosion was done in the safest manner possible.

Military and environmental officials determined that detonating it in place was the safest way to eliminate the explosive safety hazard.

The EPA, which granted an emergency permit to detonate 68 drums of the material, said it did so because the explosion risk "presented an imminent and substantial threat to human health and the environment".

One of the Environmental groups suing to pause the detonation, the Iowa Environmental Council, argued that many Iowans living within the risk-zone were unaware that the explosion was scheduled to happen.

"There is no safe level of lead exposure, and Iowans were given just days to prepare for the November 20 detonation," the organisation said in a press statement.

The Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club, which filed the lawsuit on Thursday that prompted the court-ordered pause, filed a new motion on Sunday in response to the army's filing.
sources.headline: US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order

sources.body:
The US Army plans to invoke emergency powers to detonate 4 tonnes of lead azide in an Iowa town, despite a court-ordered stay.

The United States Army intends to detonate more than 4 tonnes of lead azide at a military base in Iowa, defying a federal appeals court’s order suspending its permit to do so.

In a fact sheet this weekend, the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services said that two controlled explosions were scheduled for around noon (06:00 GMT) on Monday.

That announcement follows statements from the Department of Justice, arguing that Tuesday was the cut-off date to carry out a planned detonation.

Lead azide is a key explosive used in military ammunition. The Iowa stockpile has reportedly grown unstable, and Justice Department lawyers have warned that sub-freezing temperatures could trigger an uncontrolled explosion.

“The real choice, in other words, is not between a detonation and no detonation. It is between a planned and mitigated detonation and an unplanned and unmitigated explosion,” their court filing said.

But critics have questioned the army’s rationale for pushing ahead with the planned detonation, despite the court order to pause it.

“Anyone can claim an emergency at any point and do whatever they want. I don’t think people can or should accept that,” said Thien Chau, a lawyer with the legal group Earthjustice, which represents the plaintiffs in the lawsuit.

Chau told Al Jazeera that not enough has been done to mitigate the risk from the explosions, which are expected to release a cloud of lead into the air.

Experts say there is no safe level of lead exposure, and the dense metal can cause birth defects, brain damage and infertility.

“Anyone who hears that the army plans to explode nearly 10,000 pounds [4,500kg] of [this chemical] would recognise that that is not normal,” Chau said.

“That is extraordinary, and that is not something that you just take lightly.”

The impending explosions come after a tense legal battle between the US government and environmental groups, including the Sierra Club and the Iowa Environmental Council.

The groups have questioned the legality of an emergency permit the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) granted on November 13. The EPA authorised the Army to move forward with the explosions, originally scheduled for November 20.

The plaintiffs pointed out that nearby residents were only given a week’s notice and that the blasts could send lead dust as far as 160km (100 miles).

They also argued that the EPA failed to properly assess safer disposal methods.

The US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit granted a pause on Friday. But in a Saturday court filing, the Justice Department maintained that the Army could still proceed with the two controlled blasts under an emergency exemption.

“The emergency exception does not depend on the Emergency Permit and is therefore not affected by, nor contradictory to, the terms of this Court’s administrative stay,” the Justice Department said in its filing.

But Earthjustice has argued that such a manoeuvre would sidestep the court’s authority.
sources.headline: ‘Extremely concerning’: Inside a US Army plan to detonate Iowa lead stores

stories.headline: Windstorm injures 12 across Catalunya, including nine runners in Barcelona

sources.body:
Los servicios de emergencias en la avenida de la Meridiana de Barcelona. EFE/Alejandro Garcia

El temporal de viento que afecta a Cataluña ha dejado este domingo 12 personas heridas, de las que dos se encuentran en estado grave, ha informado Protección Civil de la Generalitat, que mantiene activo su plan de prevención VENCAT.

Según el servicio meteorológico Meteocat, el temporal dejará rachas de viento que pueden superar los 72 kilómetros por hora en buena parte del territorio, incluida Barcelona, cuyo ayuntamiento también ha activado su plan de emergencias.

En Barcelona , una persona ha quedado herida grave al caerle encima un árbol en el cruce de la calle Marina con la avenida Icària, en el barrio de la Vila Olímpica. Sanitarios del Sistema de Emergencias Médicas (SEM) han atendido en ese punto a una persona que ha sido trasladada en estado grave al Hospital del Mar .

En Matadepera (Barcelona), un árbol ha caído sobre un vehículo en la carretera BV-1221 y ha herido de gravedad a una mujer que viajaba en el mismo, que ha sido trasladada por el SEM al hospital de Terrassa (Barcelona).

La caída de otro árbol de grandes dimensiones en la confluencia de la avenida de la Meridiana con la calle de Espronceda en Barcelona ha herido a nueve mujeres que participaban en la carrera popular Cursa de les Dones (Carrera de las Mujeres), aunque ninguna de gravedad. El árbol ha caído en el momento en el que la cola de la carrera pasaba por ese punto.

El SEM ha trasladado a dos heridas al hospital de Sant Pau; otras dos al hospital Dos de Mayo, y otras dos al centro de urgencias de Sant Martí, mientras que las otras tres no han precisado traslado a un centro sanitario.

El teniente de alcalde del Ayuntamiento de Barcelona, Jordi Valls, ha informado en el lugar del suceso que se ha acordado no suspender la carrera a pesar de este accidente ya que el grueso de las corredoras ya habían pasado por ese punto y porque, para facilitar la labor de los equipos de emergencias, era mejor mantener a las participantes reagrupadas y que no se concentrasen más personas en la zona.

Ha indicado también que el árbol que ha caído se encontraba sano y que ha sido derribado por el fuerte viento. Ha precisado, en este sentido, de que la alerta lanzada por el temporal determina un grado de peligrosidad de tres en una escala de seis, lo que obliga al ayuntamiento a cerrar solo los accesos a los parques que están perimetrados, pero no a impedir el paso en las zonas ajardinadas abiertas, como en la que ha ocurrido el suceso.

Además, el viento ha derribado una farola en Sabadell (Barcelona), en la confluencia de la ronda de Bellesguard con la calle Olzinelles, y ha alcanzado a una persona que ha sido trasladada al hospital Parc Taulí de la ciudad.

El temporal ha provocado unas 350 incidencias que han obligado a actuar a los bomberos, en especial en el área metropolitana de Barcelona y en la capital catalana. Los Bomberos de la Generalitat han realizado 238 salidas —117 en el área metropolitana norte, 68 en la metropolitana sur, 32 en Tarragona, 14 en el área centro, 4 en Lleida y 3 en Girona— y los Bomberos de Barcelona, más de un centenar, la gran mayoría para cortar y retirar árboles caídos por el efecto del viento.
sources.headline: El temporal de viento en Catalu�a deja 12 personas heridas, dos de ellas en estado grave

sources.body:
Almenys dotze persones han quedat ferides , dues en estat greu, arran de l' episodi de fort vent que aquest diumenge afecta diverses comarques catalanes.

Els Bombers de la Generalitat han rebut 224 avisos relacionats amb l'episodi de vent fins a les cinc de la tarda, i els Bombers de Barcelona han fet 18 serveis . La majoria de sortides han estat relacionades amb afectacions d'arbres i amb la caiguda d'objectes a la via pública.

Fins a les cinc, el telèfon d'emergències 112 ha rebut 560 trucades per incidències relacionades amb el vent, sobretot a Barcelona i Sabadell.

El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha emès un avís de perill per fortes ratxes de vent des de les set del matí fins a la una de la matinada de dilluns en diverses comarques del litoral i prelitoral central i del sud, la Catalunya Central i el Pirineu.

En declaracions a 3CatInfo, Rosa Mata, cap de guàrdia de l'operativa de Protecció Civil , ha demanat mantenir les precaucions al llarg del dia, evitar els desplaçaments i no acostar-se a zones amb arbres o elements que puguin caure:

No podem abaixar la guàrdia, els avisos es mantenen durant la tarda.

Així mateix, en una publicació a la xarxa social X , el president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , ha demanat extremar les precaucions i evitar els desplaçaments innecessaris.

A Barcelona , una persona ha quedat ferida en estat greu a causa de la caiguda d'un arbre al parc Carles I . La persona, que havia quedat atrapada sota l'arbre, ha estat traslladada a l'Hospital del Mar de la capital catalana.

Així mateix, la caiguda d'un arbre durant la celebració de la Cursa de les Dones de Barcelona ha ferit nou participants .

En una compareixença davant dels mitjans, el quart tinent d'alcaldia de l'Ajuntament de Barcelona, Jordi Valls , ha explicat que la cursa no s'havia suspès perquè en el cas d' avisos de nivell 3 sobre 6 , com l'actual, no es preveu fer-ho.

També a la capital catalana, el vent ha tornat a destrossar les làmines de vidre de la instal·lació "Pavelló-Laberint", que s'havien reinstal·lat al pavelló Mies van der Rohe després que el vent les fes malbé fa només deu dies .

El vent destrossa un altre cop la instal·lació amb 300 làmines de vidre al pavelló Mies van der Rohe. Ara fa una setmana les ventades van trencar la intervenció artística "Pavelló-Laberint", que s'acabava d'inaugurar https://t.co/XE2Xjx3ODi https://t.co/IlF3V6yKy4

A Matadepera , al Vallès Occidental, una persona ha quedat ferida greu arran de la caiguda d'un arbre sobre un vehicle. L'incident ha tingut lloc a la carretera BV-1221.

Fins al lloc dels fets s'hi ha traslladat una ambulància i una dotació dels Bombers. La dona ha estat traslladada a l' Hospital de Terrassa .

D'altra banda, a Sabadell , al Vallès Occidental, ha caigut un fanal i ha deixat una altra persona ferida.

A Rubí , a la mateixa comarca, l'Ajuntament ha desallotjat el pavelló de Can Rosés després que una placa de la teulada caigués sobre el camp de futbol adjacent. Els Bombers s'hi han desplaçat i han retirat altres planxes de la teulada que estaven inestables i la policia ha acordonat l'equipament.
sources.headline: Alerta per ventades: dotze ferits, dos de greus, i desenes d'incidències per arbres i objectes caiguts

sources.body: Una desena de persones , una de les quals en estat greu , han resultat ferides aquest diumenge per la caiguda de branques de dos arbres com a conseqüència del vent a la ciutat. El primer incident s’ha produït cap a les 10 h a l’avinguda Meridiana i ha deixat 9 participants de la Cursa de les Dones ferides lleus . El segon incident ha tingut lloc al Parc de Carles I i ha deixat un home en estat greu. També et pot interessar Barcelona tanca els parcs i jardins de la ciutat per l’episodi de vent Jessica Moreno Cusac 1 minut de lectura Sis de les ferides, traslladades a centres de salut Segons ha explicat el tinent d’alcaldia Jordi Valls, l’incident de la Cursa de les Dones ha tingut lloc a la part final de la competició. Des del consistori, però, s’ha decidit mantenir la cursa perquè s’ha considerat que, des del punt de vista de seguretat, era millor mantenir tot el grup de corredores unit . Valls també ha afegit que el nivell d’alerta de Protecció Civil era de grau 3 sobre 6, un nivell que no requereix la suspensió d’activitats a l’aire lliure. Fins al lloc dels fets s’hi han desplaçat sis dotacions del Sistema d’Emergències Mèdiques, els Mossos d’Esquadra i la Guàrdia Urbana i els Bombers de Barcelona. Segons ha informat el SEM, dues persones han estat traslladades al CUAP Sant Martí; dues, a l’Hospital Dos de Maig, i dues més, a l’Hospital de Sant Pau. Les altres tres no han requerit ser traslladades a cap centre hospitalari. Com a conseqüència d’aquest incident s’ha tallat l’avinguda Meridiana d’entrada a la ciutat. També et pot interessar Protecció Civil activa l’alerta per ratxes de vent de més de 70 km/h a Barcelona i demana precaució Jessica Moreno Cusac 1 minut de lectura Un ferit greu al Parc de Carles I Un altre arbre ha caigut al Parc de Carles I , a l’avinguda d’Icària amb el carrer de la Marina, i ha deixat una altra persona ferida . Es tracta d’un home que ha estat traslladat en estat greu a l’Hospital del Mar. El consistori ha apuntat que, en tots dos casos, els arbres estaven al corrent de les revisions periòdiques i tenien un estat normal. També et pot interessar Ratxes de vent de fins a 84 km/h a Gràcia i 73 km/h a Sant Andreu aquest diumenge Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 2 minuts de lectura Més d’un centenar d’actuacions dels Bombers Entre les 8 i les 14 h, els Bombers de Barcelona han realitzat 107 serveis relacionats amb el vent . Per la seva banda, els Bombers de la Generalitat han atès 224 avisos fins a les 17 h. La majoria de les intervencions han estan relacionades amb arbres i altres elements caiguts a la via pública. Un dels més importants s’ha registrat a Matadepera després que un arbre hagi caigut sobre un vehicle . Com a conseqüència, la conductora ha resultat ferida greu. També hi ha un altre ferit, en aquest cas lleu, a Sabadell per la caiguda d’un fanal.
sources.headline: Una desena de ferits, un dels quals greu, per la caiguda de branques d’arbres pel vent

stories.headline: Passeig de Gràcia faces four days of closures for Christmas-light preparations

sources.body:
L'Ajuntament de Barcelona farà l'encesa dels llums de Nadal dijous, 26 de novembre, a la tarda i la preparació de tot plegat es notarà a partir d'aquest dilluns , amb el passeig de Gràcia tallat al trànsit i amb canvis al transport públic.

Els talls al tronc central del passeig afectaran els dos sentits de la circulació en diferents trams i s'estendran a tot el passeig, entre la Diagonal i la Gran Via, a partir de les dues del migdia del dia de l'acte.

Dilluns 23 hi ha les primeres afectacions a partir de les deu del matí .

En sentit mar , queda tallat el tronc central del passeig de Gràcia entre l'avinguda Diagonal i el carrer Provença.

En sentit muntanya , el tall és entre el carrer Aragó i la Diagonal.

En canvi, es mantindran oberts els laterals del passeig de Gràcia i l'avinguda Diagonal i el carrer Provença.

Dijous 26 , coincidint amb l'acte d'encesa, les restriccions s'ampliaran a partir de les 14.00 h i fins que s'hagi buidat de públic.

Tot el passeig quedarà tallat al trànsit entre la Diagonal i la Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes, en tots dos sentits.

També es tancaran els carrers transversals , excepte la Diagonal, els carrers Aragó i Diputació i la Gran Via. Aquests carrers, però, també es podran tallar en funció de l'afluència de públic per garantir-ne la seguretat.

Les línies 22 i 24 del bus es veuen afectades en tots dos sentits i les línies 7 i V15 ho estan en sentit muntanya. Els autobusos es desviaran per carrers propers des de dilluns, dia 23, i fins divendres, dia 27, a les 8.00 h. També el Nitbus i el Bus Turístic queden afectats.

A més, dijous, dia 26 , a partir de les 17.00 h es tancaran els accessos del metro a la zona afectada.

El servei de Bicing també tindrà alteracions. L'estació 374, situada al passeig de Gràcia entre el carrer Provença i el passatge de la Concepció, queda fora de servei des de dilluns a les 6.00 h fins divendres a les 8.00 h.

L'estació 465, al carrer Rosselló, prop de la cantonada amb el passeig de Gràcia, continuarà operativa fins dimecres i tancarà durant tot dijous, dia 26 .

Per assistir a l'espectacle de dijous a la tarda es recomana utilitzar estacions de metro alternatives a les més properes a l'escenari. Entre les opcions indicades hi ha Catalunya (L1 i L3), Fontana (L3) i Verdaguer (L4 i L5).

L'enllumenat de Nadal estarà encès a Barcelona des del 26 de novembre fins al 6 de gener, ambdós inclosos, amb aquests horaris : de diumenge a dijous, des de les 17.30 fins a la 1.00 h; els divendres i dissabtes des de les 17:30 fins a les 2:00 h, i els dies extraordinaris, com el 24, 25 i 31 de desembre i 5 de gener, també de 17:30 a 2:00 h.
sources.headline: Tallen quatre dies el passeig de Gràcia de Barcelona per l'encesa dels llums de Nadal

sources.body:
Una calle de Barcelona decorada con luces de Navidad bajo el lema "Vens per Nadal". / Ayuntamiento de Barcelona

Las tareas para montar las luces de Navidad en el tramo central de paseo de Gràcia obligarán a interrumpir el tráfico entre avenida Diagonal y la calle Provença en sentido mar y entre la calle Aragó y Diagonal en sentido montaña , entre los días 23 y 26 de noviembre, ha informado el Ayuntamiento de Barcelona.

Los trabajos también obligarán a cortar la calle Rosselló, mientras que Diagonal, Provença y los laterales de paseo de Gràcia se mantendrán abiertos al tráfico.

El día 26 por la tarde, el corte se extenderá a todo el paseo de Gràcia, desde la avenida Diagonal hasta la Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes en ambos sentidos con motivo del espectáculo previsto para la inauguración de las luces navideñas.

El servicio de autobús quedará afectado también desde el 23 de noviembre , y no recuperará la normalidad hasta el viernes 27. Las líneas afectadas, que se desviarán por calles cercanas, serán la 22 y la 24 en ambos sentidos, y la 7 y la V15 solo en sentido montaña.

Por otro lado, los accesos al metro de la zona afectada quedarán cerrados el día 26 a partir de las 17 horas . Se podrán utilizar o tras estaciones más alejadas de la zona del espectáculo, como Catalunya (L1, L3), Fontana (L3) o Verdaguer (L4, L5).

Por último, la estación de Bicing situada entre la calle de Provença y el pasaje de la Concepció estará fuera de servicio desde el lunes 23 y hasta el viernes 27. La estación 465 de la calle de Rosselló, se mantendrá operativa hasta el mismo día del encendido, el jueves 26
sources.headline: Cortes de tráfico y cambios en el transporte público en Barcelona desde este lunes por el montaje de las luces de Navidad
